rationale:
The tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`.

- **Whole-file outline when one item is selected.**
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` selects the line `second` from a file whose outline has three items. It asserts that `selected.outline().items.len() == 3`, so the outline is the whole file's outline and not just the selection's.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` asserts `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` for a selected section.
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts the same pointer equality for a selected function.
  - The same markdown test calls `second.select(main)` on the selected content and resolves a sibling item, which shows the full outline is retained.
- **Root first, then items in source preorder.**
  - The Rust test asserts the exact selector and kind sequence `""`, `mod[auth]`, `mod[auth]/fn[check]`, `mod[auth]/struct[Token]`, `fn[last]`. This checks root first, children after their parent, and the later top-level sibling after the whole subtree.
  - The markdown test asserts the ordered list of section selectors, including nested and duplicate (`#1`, `#2`) sections.
  - The setext test asserts the ordered section selectors for its source.
  - The unknown-extension and unicode tests assert the order of line items after the root.
- **Root has an empty selector and covers the whole source snapshot.**
  - `items[0].span` is asserted to be `Span::new(0, source.len())` in the Rust, markdown and unicode tests.
  - The unknown-extension test asserts `Span::new(0, 18)`.
  - The unknown-extension test also asserts that an empty file has a single root item with span `(0, 0)`.
  - The unicode test asserts `items[0].selector == ""`. The Rust test asserts `""` as the first selector.
- **Full selectors identify items and their ancestry** (cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`). The Rust test asserts nested selectors such as `mod[auth]/fn[check]`. The markdown tests assert encoded names, `#N` duplicate disambiguation, and anonymous `block@`/`section@` segments under their ancestors. The unknown-extension test asserts `line@` hash segments and that duplicate lines share a selector.

I found no obligation without a test, and no assertion that contradicts the text.

text: :::{req} items
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
The root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.
